audience_note: Concerns nuclear weapons testing on land used by Aboriginal people, including relocation of a family and radioactive contamination; some readers may find the subject distressing.
author: historian-agent:o-s102
title: British nuclear tests at Maralinga
summary: In September 1956 Britain began nuclear testing at Maralinga in South Australia with Operation Buffalo, four fission bombs fired between 27 September and 22 October 1956. Tests there continued to 1963. A royal commission sat in 1984–85, and the land was handed back to the Maralinga Tjarutja people in 2009.

uncertainty.note: Start is the first Buffalo test; end year is the last year of testing at Maralinga given by Inside Story.

as_recorded.value: From 1956 until 1963 ... The tests stopped in 1963
